article_sentences: Guwahati: As preparations for Durga Puja gather pace across Assam, the inspiring story of a differently abled artisan from Cachar district has captured attention.
Montu Pal, a resident of Siddheswar village in Katigorah, has been crafting Durga idols for the past 18 years, overcoming severe physical challenges through determination and dedication to his art.
Pal lost both his legs in a horrific train accident several years ago.
While the tragedy could have shattered his spirit, it failed to diminish his passion for idol-making.
Undeterred by his physical limitations, he continued his artistic journey, working on his knees and crawling to shape clay into beautifully crafted idols.
Throughout this challenging journey, Pal has received unwavering support from his family.
His wife and children have stood firmly by his side, assisting him at every stage of the idol-making process.
Their contribution has enabled him to continue pursuing his craft despite the difficulties he faces.
This year, Pal has created 16 Durga idols entirely by hand for the upcoming festival, reflecting his exceptional craftsmanship and perseverance.
However, rising prices of raw materials have added to his financial difficulties.
The cost of essential materials, including paint, bamboo, straw, sand and clay, has reportedly nearly doubled, significantly increasing the expenses involved in making the idols.
Despite these challenges, Pal remains committed to his work.

stories.headline: Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted in India’s presidential election
stories.title: Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted in India’s presidential election
stories.summary: The claim came while Trump criticised the time taken to count votes in several US cities and states, calling voting corrupt
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In an apparent faux pas, US President Donald Trump mentioned India in a social media post to claim that the electoral process in the US was “corrupt”, when there were no elections in India, and the post clearly appeared to be about the presidential election in Brazil.
In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump claimed that “125 million people voted in India’s Presidential elections and the results came out shortly after the vote closed”.
“Voting in America is CORRUPT,” Trump said, referring to the weeks taken for the counting of votes in elections in US cities and states.
“125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election.
The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the SAME DAY,” Trump said.
“In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate.
Voting in America is CORRUPT,” the US president said.
The reference to India appeared to be a possible mix-up with Brazil.
Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with 125.27 million valid votes recorded, according to the country’s electoral authority.
Results began to be released at 5 pm, when voting ended, and were updated as ballots were received and processed.
Brazilians voted in the presidential election pitting incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.
With neither of them able to secure a majority in the first round, the run-off election will be held on October 25.

article_sentences: RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has approached the Supreme Court challenging the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, terming it a "fraud" on the Constitution.

Section 16 bars every Court in the country from entertaining or continuing any civil or criminal proceeding against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner, for anything done "or purporting" to be done in the discharge of official duty.

Jha has stated that Section 16 confers on unelected officials a shield/blanket immunity which is not even extended to the President, Governor, Member of Parliament, State Legislature, or any judge of the Supreme Court or the High Court, because the immunity extends for a lifetime.
This was added through an amendment in 2023, which had also removed the pro tem arrangement made by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal.

Union of India(2023) for the appointment of the CEC by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party), and the Chief Justice of India.
The 2023 Act had removed the CJI and added a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

Jha's petition argues: "Parliament, by a late official amendment to an ordinary Bill, has handed the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners a protection wider than all of them: civil and criminal, during office and for life after it, with no carve-out for corruption, mala fides or crime, and with no authority anywhere empowered to lift it."
Jha has stated that Section 16, added through an amendment, is a fraud on the Constitution because it was not originally provided in the Act.
He has said that wherever the Constitutional framers thought fit to provide functional immunity, it has done so and that too only till the person is holding the office.
Per contra, no such immunity was provided under Section 324 of the Constitution for the protection of the Election Commission.
"Section 16 nonetheless confers a constitutional-grade immunity, larger than any the Constitution grants or permits, through a simple majority statute.
It does so under the label of "conditions of service" in an Act whose long title speaks only of "appointment, conditions of service and term of office" and "transaction of business".

stories.headline: “Any terror act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response”: Rajnath Singh
stories.title: “Any terror act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response”: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi , October 15 : Reiterating India’s stand on cross-border terrorism, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday asserted that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response. He emphasised that while India’s cultural ethos favoured dialogue, coexistence and peaceful resolution of disputes, its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for weakness. “Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Singh said at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi. He added that since 2014, the ‘shelf life’ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India. Defence Minister termed strength and capability as essential to maintaining peace, and underlined that India hopes for peace, but remains prepared for war that sometimes becomes necessary to protect the nation. “Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge. Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said. On the evolving security landscape, Singh underscored the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness in an era of hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare. He highlighted the growing complexity of security threats in the digital age, identifying what he described as the ‘5D Security Threat ’-Disinformation, Destabilisation, Disruption, Deception and Destruction. He pointed out that terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, and emerging threats include ‘lone-wolf’ attacks and ‘white-collar terrorism’, which make it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks. The Defence Minister referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Captain Smit Machhar who risked his life to avert a major terror attack. “The incident underscored the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers while demonstrating how the courage and commitment of an individual could thwart the designs of those driven by hatred. A single alert and courageous individual could help foil an entire terrorist plot. The fight against terrorism requires not only the capabilities of security agencies but also the active participation of aware and responsible citizens,” he said. On defence preparedness, Singh underscored the need to combine ‘hard power’ with ‘soft power’ and called for a shift towards ‘smart power’. “Modern defence strategies must integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with cost-effective weaponry, human intelligence with artificial intelligence, and advanced systems with low-cost, agile and adaptable technologies to address evolving security challenges,” he said. On the growth witnessed by the defence sector due to the Government’s efforts, Singh stated that defence production has risen to a record over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, with defence exports touching an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and India defence products reaching nearly 100 countries. He exuded confidence that the nation would achieve defence production targets of Rs 2 lakh crore this year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, and export defence equipment worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029, the Ministry said in its statement. The Defence Minister attributed the growth to reforms that simplified export procedures, including the introduction of the Defence EXIM Portal, online approvals, the Open General Export License, streamlined quality certification and the ‘Green Channel’ policy. These measures, he said, enhanced India’s global credibility and prepared domestic industries to compete in international markets. "The Ministry of Defence has approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects exceeding Rs 1,500 crore for new technology development. As of March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups and innovators and facilitated the signing of 551 contracts. From a few dozen defence startups in 2018, the ecosystem had grown to more than 2,000, with young enterprises working across drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity, robotics and other advanced fields,” he added. Citing progress in ammunition manufacturing, he said 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the Defence Forces were now indigenously produced, representing more than 90 per cent self-reliance in ammunition variants. Referring to India’s exports of bulletproof jackets to over 100 countries, he noted that the country was the fourth in the world to establish a national standard for bulletproof jackets aligned with international norms. He also spoke about the implementation of the One Rank One Pension scheme and the creation of the Chief of Defence Staff post, terming them significant measures undertaken to strengthen the defence framework.

stories.title: Big items done, confident we will have India-US trade deal: Sergio Gor

Within three weeks of [Gor’s] arriving here, we announced a trade deal,” Gor said.The US Supreme Court then ruled that the tariffs were unconstitutional. “The administration has had to go back and rework some of those things. So we’re getting there,” he added. They’re literally discussing percentages of products. It’s down to that kind of detail,” he explained.India signed a trade deal with the European Union earlier this year, which was concluded after 20 years of negotiations. India and the US have been in talks for one-and-a-half years. “We’re at an incredible pace, and I would say almost an unheard-of pace. stories.summary: Leh, Oct 15: Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena hailed the Centre's initiatives on Thursday after Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated five development projects in Ladakh, including airport infrastructure and strategic road connectivity, worth around Rs 3,350 crore. Saxena said the region has seen a major transformation in infrastructure and living standards under the Prime Minister's leadership since it became a Union Territory in 2019. Saxena said, "Five new infrastructure projects would prove to be milestones in Ladakh's development, strengthening connectivity, water security, power supply and preservation of cultural heritage." The Lieutenant Governor (LG) thanked Narendra Modi for his leadership and support, saying the people of Ladakh's seven districts looked forward to his address with high hopes and aspirations. The Prime Minister inaugurated five projects, including a modern passenger terminal at Leh airport; the Nimmu-Padam-Darcha road connecting the Zanskar valley; India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park in Leh; the 9 MW Hanu Hydroelectric Project; and power transmission infrastructure and 35 water bodies under the Amrit Sarovar initiative. "The inauguration of the Banga Bot Kharu Small Hydroelectric Project and the 66-kV Thahanu-Khalsti transmission line will also help strengthen the region's power infrastructure," the LG said. Saxena said the new airport terminal would improve air connectivity and passenger facilities, particularly during winter, while the Nimmu-Padam-Darcha road would connect remote areas with the mainstream of development and strengthen internal security. Highlighting 2019, he said granting Ladakh Union Territory status fulfilled a long-standing demand for a distinct identity and greater recognition. "The formation of five new districts in April this year and the recent approval for establishing Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all seven districts were important steps towards fulfilling local aspirations," he said. Saxena said Ladakh was improving road connectivity and other infrastructure, while work under the Jal Jeevan Mission was progressing to provide clean drinking water to households despite sub-zero temperatures. He said new policies were also being introduced to economically empower Pashmina herders, while agricultural diversification was helping increase farmers' incomes. The LG said Ladakh, which once depended on outside supplies for vegetables, now has more than 11,000 greenhouses where farmers grow vegetables locally and supply them to defence forces through cooperatives. Emphasising the importance of water conservation, Saxena said initiatives such as Amrit Him Sarovar and conserving glacial water resources were helping ensure long-term water security in the strategically important region. Improved connectivity, infrastructure development, and ease of doing business have also boosted tourism and strengthened the local economy, he said. The LG said the Zojila Tunnel's completion would address one of Ladakh's major connectivity challenges, as the region often remains cut off from the rest of the country during winter due to heavy snowfall. Work on the tunnel is progressing on a war footing, he said, and he requested the Prime Minister to inaugurate the project once it was completed. Saxena expressed confidence that Ladakh would continue to receive the Prime Minister's guidance and support for its overall development. He welcomed Modi on behalf of the Ladakh administration and its people, thanking him for participating in the programme despite being unable to visit the region in person. "The snow-covered peaks and the inaccessible valleys of Ladakh have always symbolised courage and perseverance. However, under the leadership of the Prime Minister, these very challenges have now become symbols of development and new hope," Saxena said. He said Modi's decision to join the programme virtually reflected his affection for the people of Ladakh, his dedication to their welfare and his vision for the region. Saxena said the people of Ladakh would remain grateful to the Prime Minister for sparing his valuable time to honour them and give unprecedented momentum to the region's development. Ladakh is home to hundreds of prehistoric rock art sites featuring carvings of wildlife, human figures and symbolic representations that offer valuable insights into thousands of years of human history.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has flagged an “undesirable incident” involving the alleged use of AI-generated, non-existent judgments in a compilation of cases submitted on behalf of the appellants, expressing concern over the conduct of the lawyers involved in the matter.
A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih, while dismissing appeals filed by GSTAAD Hotels Pvt.
and Neo Capricorn Plaza Pvt.
against the initiation of insolvency proceedings against them, recorded that the respondents had immediately objected to the compilation, alleging that it contained judgments that did not exist.

“When queried by the Court, the Advocate-on-Record for the appellants sought to shift the entire blame on the appellants while at the same time feigning ignorance of what the compilation contained,” the Court observed.
The judgment further recorded that senior counsel appearing for the appellants subsequently took responsibility for the incident and sought forgiveness on behalf of the appellants.

The Court had initially considered imposing exemplary costs but, after being informed of the death of the first appellant, deleted the proposed costs and directed that there would be no order as to costs.

The Court made these observations while deciding appeals filed by the companies challenging the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal's decision upholding the admission of insolvency petitions under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC).

On the merits, the Supreme Court held that at the admission stage of an insolvency petition, a financial creditor is required to establish the occurrence of default through a summary assessment of documentary evidence and need not prove the exact outstanding liability after an exhaustive reconciliation of the corporate debtor's accounts.
“The trigger for initiation of the CIRP is the occurrence of a default, not the final adjudication of the creditor's entire claim,” the Court said.

The Bench clarified that disputes over the precise amount of outstanding debt, including the computation of interest, penal charges or other accounting entries, do not negate an established default or prevent admission of a Section 7 application, provided the statutory threshold under Section 4 of the IBC is satisfied.

“The standard applicable at the admission stage is one of preponderance of probabilities upon the documentary material placed on record,” the Court observed, adding that the threshold was deliberately modest and required a summary, prima facie finding of financial debt and default rather than a full trial into disputed facts.

article_sentences: Union Minister Amit Shah on Saturday (October 3, 2026) said in Bhopal that criminal cases in the country will be completed within three years, even if they go all the way to the Supreme Court, once the new criminal laws are fully implemented.
Mr. Shah, who is also the Minister for Cooperation, was speaking at a cattle rearers’ conference, ‘Gaupalak Sammelan’, in the capital of Madhya Pradesh.
Along with Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, he also inaugurated a state-level exhibition on the new criminal codes at Bhopal’s BHEL Dussehra ground.
“Our justice system was once known for its ‘tareekh pe tareekh (date after date)’ taunts.

Once the laws are fully implemented in one to one-and-a-half years, whatever FIR (first information report) you file, the culprit will be punished within three years, up to the Supreme Court,” he said, adding that the old codes were made by the British to protect their rule.
“Now, the new laws have been made to protect the honour, property and body of the Indian public.
Their mool mantra (fundamental principle) is justice.
After their full implementation, our criminal justice system will become the most modern system in the world.

We have integrated various modern scientific technologies in it, like digital evidence, e-summons, online hearings, video conferencings and various provisions related to FSL (forensic science laboratories),” the Union Minister said.
“There are provisions for women’s safety, [finding] missing children and protection from terrorism and lynching in them,” Mr. Shah added.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has observed that it would be “highly unfair” to make investors bear the consequences of administrative lapses, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) allegedly allowed YES Bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio to fall to 0.6% despite earlier irregularities in the bank's functioning.
“The RBI was a mere bystander, allowing the CET1 ratio of YES BANK to drop to an astonishing low of 0.6% while the business of YES BANK was being carried out in a clandestine manner.
It cannot be denied that material irregularities in functioning of YES BANK were noticed much prior; criminal prosecution has also been initiated against the personnel of YES BANK.

However, to have the investors at the receiving end of the administrative lapses would be highly unfair.”, a bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih observed while setting aside the write-down of ₹8,415 crore worth of Additional Tier 1 (AT-1) bonds.
The Court upheld the Bombay High Court's decision, holding that YES Bank's Administrator lacked the authority to write down the bonds after the final reconstruction scheme came into force.
“…administrator appointed under the BR Act has to act squarely within the four corners of the powers conferred upon him under the statute.
He acts as a substitute for the Board of Directors, to run the company in an efficient manner.

Any act performed by the administrator beyond the powers clothed upon him would be wholly illegal and void.”, the Court said, emphasizing that an Administrator cannot be said to have exercised the power vested in the RBI.
The Court noted that material irregularities in YES Bank's functioning had been noticed much earlier and criminal prosecution had also been initiated against bank personnel.
However, it said investors could not be made to bear the consequences of administrative failures.
Although the draft reconstruction scheme expressly provided for a permanent write-down of AT-1 bonds, the clause was omitted from the final scheme notified on March 13, 2020.
The Administrator nevertheless wrote down the bonds the next day, extinguishing investors' claims.

stories.headline: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.title: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15 : India's merchandise exports recorded a robust 23.04 per cent growth year-on-year to touch a four-month high of $44.4 billion in September this year, despite the uncertainties in global markets and the disruption in shipping due to the escalating Middle East conflict, official figures released on Thursday showed. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said the growth trend in India's exports was continuing, indicating sustained momentum in outbound shipments. The growth in goods exports was driven by a broad-based increase in shipments across sectors, with particularly strong growth in petroleum products, meat, dairy and poultry products, handicrafts, and some cereals, he added. Imports rose 8 per cent to $74.61 billion during the month due to the increase in prices of crude oil in the global market. The surge in exports also led to a narrowing of the trade deficit to $30.21 billion during the month on a year-on-year basis from around $33 billion recorded in September 2025. However, on a sequential basis, the trade deficit was higher than the corresponding figure of $26.86 billion in the previous month of August. Cumulatively, goods exports stood at $259.89 billion during April-September, up nearly 19 per cent year-on-year. Imports rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $437.53 billion in the first six months of financial year 2026-27 (FY27). As a result, the merchandise trade deficit stood at $177.64 billion during the six-month period. Strong growth in merchandise exports has also increased their contribution to gross domestic product (GDP), after the share of exports recorded a consistent decline over the past three financial years. Exports accounted for 14 per cent of GDP in the first quarter of FY27, the latest figures show. Following a slowdown in global demand in FY24 and FY25, and the uncertainties triggered by the US tariff turmoil in FY26, the share of exports in GDP declined to 11.3 per cent in FY26 from 11.7 per cent in FY25. --IANS

stories.headline: Supreme Court Sets Aside Gift Deed Executed Over Share Given Up In Family Settlement
stories.title: Supreme Court Sets Aside Gift Deed Executed Over Share Given Up In Family Settlement
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has held that a person having parted with his share in a property via a compromise deed cannot later execute a gift deed in relation to the same property.

The Court faulted the Telangana High Court's order for overlooking a compromise deed before upholding the execution of a gift deed by a man who had already relinquished his share via a compromise deed.

A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva heard a case in which a man, despite having relinquished his claim over properties allotted to his mother under a 1986 compromise in exchange for absolute rights over a house property, subsequently executed a gift deed in 2007 in respect of the same properties.

The core legal issue before the Court was whether a gift deed could be upheld without properly appreciating the effect of an earlier family settlement and a compromise decree that had recognised the parties' respective rights over the properties.
The dispute arose from a family settlement executed on April 19, 1959, dividing ancestral properties among family members.
Under the settlement, Madhusudhan Reddy received specific properties, while certain lands in Karkalpahad village were allotted to his mother, Manikyamma.
Subsequently, during the pendency of litigation concerning the family properties, Madhusudhan Reddy entered into a compromise with Anasuyamma and her adopted son, Venkatraji Reddy, in February 1986.
Under the settlement, he relinquished his claim over the properties allotted to his mother and secured absolute rights over the Himayatnagar house.
The compromise was recorded by the High Court, which allowed the appeal in terms of the settlement in September 1990.
However, in April 2007, Madhusudhan Reddy executed a registered gift deed in favour of Siddhartha Reddy, transferring several parcels of land in Karkalpahad village.

The appellants contended that the lands covered by the deed had not been allotted to Madhusudhan Reddy under the 1959 family settlement and were among the properties over which he had relinquished his claims under the 1986 compromise.

Anasuyamma, Venkatraji Reddy and another family member subsequently filed a suit seeking a declaration of title, a declaration that the gift deed was null and void, mutation of revenue records and a permanent injunction.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has criticised the manner in which the Allahabad High Court has dealt with a case while granting probation to two men convicted for a brutal attack that left a victim with grievous injuries.
The Court said that the accused were released on probation in ignorance of the adverse report submitted by the probation officer against them.
“The High Court, despite the overwhelming adverse report on the 'character of the offenders' and giving short shrift to the 'nature of the offence', released the accused on good conduct.

There was nothing commending the Court to so release the accused, since the conduct, over the years, of the accused was anything other than 'good'.”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, adding that despite the brutality of the attack and the serious injuries suffered by the victim, “the accused have gone scot-free without suffering a single day of imprisonment…”.
The case arose from a 2003 incident in which the two accused allegedly attacked the victim with a cutting weapon and a firearm following a dispute involving neighbouring shops.
The victim suffered cut injuries and gunshot wounds and continues to experience debilitating consequences of the assault.
The trial court convicted the accused under Section 308 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced them to five years' rigorous imprisonment with a fine of ₹20,000 each.

The High Court upheld the conviction but extended the benefit of Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (“PoO Act”), directing the accused to execute personal bonds of ₹20,000 each and maintain peace and good behaviour for one year.
The High Court relied on the passage of approximately 22 years since the incident and the absence of previous convictions.
Aggrieved by the High Court's order, the informant (brother of the victim) moved to the Supreme Court.

It observed that the injuries, on a plain reading, fell within the definition of grievous hurt under Section 320 IPC and that the offence ought to have been charged under Section 307 IPC rather than Section 308 IPC.

Possibly the entry of the remarks of the learned Single Judge in the Annual Confidential Report (ACR) would have sufficed.

We have also stated, the petitioner/judicial officer could have been counseled and warned to be more careful in future and to give sufficient weightage to the orders of the High Court particularly when the same were passed earlier in the same case by the High Court.

In the circumstance, we find that the Memorandum dated 25.10.2024 at Annexure P-6, the statement of charges under Rule 16 of the Rules, the allegation of charge etc. were not warranted for in the instant case.”, the Court held.

Accordingly, the Court quashed the disciplinary memorandum dated October 25, 2024, and the related charges.

stories.title: Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
stories.summary: Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.

Jio Platforms plans to raise revenue per customer mainly by selling more services rather than lifting tariffs, though it keeps the option of higher prices, Managing Director Akash Ambani said on Thursday, days before the Reliance Industries unit opens what would be India's largest initial public offering.

"We always have the ability to take up prices," Ambani told a press conference in Mumbai, but the company would rather give customers more services and charge for them than rely on price per gigabyte as its main lever.
Asked whether a tariff increase was coming, he gave no timeline.
He said telecom spending per user as a share of India's per-capita income had roughly halved to about 1% since Jio's 2016 launch, which he called headroom.
Chief Executive Pankaj Pawar said tariffs were only one of several levers.

"We expect a USD 1.4-trillion digital economy by FY31; we will take a huge market share of this," Ambani said, naming mobile, home broadband and enterprise and international services as the growth engines.
He said Jio carries more than 60% of India's wireless data traffic.
New services outside Jio's licensed telecom business, such as a voice-AI feature announced at Reliance's annual meeting, could push its EBITDA margin above the current level.
The margin was 53.3 per cent in April-June, up from about 50% three years ago, he added.

On overseas expansion, Ambani said Jio would offer its in-house network technology to foreign operators as a managed-service partner, not by selling hardware or software licences, and without heavy capital spending.
He said the split between domestic and international revenue would become clear "as we sign on our first customers".
